header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 50 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Riley Chen (Redwood SE), Dana Lopez (CTO, NovaHealth), Michael Huang (Platform Engineer, NovaHealth), Priya Singh (Security, NovaHealth)
summary: Quick sync on POC status: network peering issues partly resolved, initial perf numbers improved with batching/quant. Still seeing intermittent p95 latency spikes during KV cache misses and routing lag during autoscaling. Security asks: SOC2 evidence, SAML flow verification, KMS principals. Next steps: share network diagram, run extended perf (10k), schedule on-prem install window, deliver tuned configs.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: ok hey team thanks for joining the weekly pilot sync, we've got about 50 minutes so we'll walk through logs, perf, and outstanding security/network items.
[00:22] Dana: thanks, Samir. we've got platform, security and infra on the call to make decisions.
[00:32] Riley: i'll start with the perf summary — ran the tuned batching job across the pilot cluster yesterday. p50 ~48ms, p95 ~420ms, throughput up ~20% vs last week with batch sizing at 8-12. we did observe intermittent spikes up to ~900ms during certain long-context requests.
[01:00] Michael: that's consistent with what we saw — spikes correlate with cache-miss patterns and times when pods are scaling. our logs show obvious routing hops back to the public path for a small subset.
[01:20] Riley: yeah that routing shunt happens during rapid autoscale when the new pod isn't in the local route table yet; kube-proxy and our custom routing reconciler lag by a few seconds under churn. we patched a reconciler tweak in the canary last night.
[01:38] Priya: pause — on the peering change you asked us to make, can you confirm whether any IP range changes will affect SAML endpoints or the key policies? our compliance team flagged that as high priority.
[01:52] Samir: good question. SAML endpoint hostnames shouldn't change; however for KMS you're right — we need to update allowed_principals for the service account from your side. we'll provide exact CIDRs and principals.
[02:10] Dana: please get those to us. also what's the status of that runtime build you mentioned?
[02:18] Riley: build 2.1.4 was deployed to the pilot cluster — it includes improved KV cache eviction heuristics and a kernel path that reduces allocator stalls. initial metric smoothing is positive but we need a full 10k run under controlled conditions to validate.
[02:40] Michael: can we do that run next Tuesday during our maintenance window?
[02:44] Samir: Tuesday works, we'll reserve nodes and coordinate. reminder: we need peering and traceroute proofs before the run so we can confirm routing.
[02:56] Michael: noted, i'll collect and share the traceroutes and VPC peering logs by Monday.
[03:02] Priya: security docs — SOC2 evidences, network diagrams and audit log retention. what's in the pack?
[03:10] Samir: we'll share a security pack containing SOC2 summary, KMS integration notes (including rotation and principals), audit log retention options and sample SSO flow diagrams.
[03:22] Priya: also we require periodic key rotation and want to confirm whether Redwood's private deployment supports customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed.
[03:30] Riley: we support both; for your pilot we can use customer KMS via cross-account grants. we'll include the exact policy snippet in the security pack.
[03:42] Dana: great. back to perf — Riley you mentioned quantization gave lower latency but some small diffs in output?
[03:50] Riley: correct. using the q4 quant profile reduced per-token latency, especially at higher concurrency, but on a subset of evaluation prompts the completions drifted slightly in wording. nothing catastrophic, but for clinical notes we should be conservative.
[04:06] Michael: accuracy is non-negotiable for our use-case. what's your validation plan to avoid regressions?
[04:12] Riley: propose an A/B evaluation: we run your redacted prompt set across float and q4 quant, compute embedding similarity and token-level diffs, plus manual spot checks on clinically sensitive prompts. we'll produce a short report.
[04:28] Dana: we'll prepare a small redacted sample and put it in the drive by EOD Friday.
[04:34] Samir: perfect. another ops note: we saw 502s during scale-down events. Riley mentioned graceful shutdown tuning?
[04:44] Riley: yes, we've increased preStop drain to 25s and added a graceful shutdown handler in the runtime that flushes in-flight streams to the KV cache. that reduced 502s in canary but your LB health-check interval is short — currently set to 10s — extending to 30s would help.
[05:02] Michael: we can extend to 30s in staging and monitor.
[05:06] Priya: any implications for request retry semantics? some of our client libs retry on 5xx, which could double-load the system.
[05:14] Riley: good point — increasing client-side jitter and exponential backoff is recommended. we'll share suggested retry configs.
[05:24] Samir: on routing fallbacks: we do have a hosted fallback tier that keeps apps online if private capacity is exhausted. we left it off for your pilot due to data residency concerns. we can simulate load without enabling fallback for the 10k run.
[05:40] Dana: prefer to keep fallback off for any prod-like tests. for non-prod, maybe ok but would require DPA updates.
[05:48] Samir: understood. we'll keep fallback disabled for your perf window.
[05:54] Riley: small config note — for your prompt lengths the best batch size we found was 8–12. going to 16 increased cold-start latency and raised p95. also prefix/KV cache length affects hit-rate; we tuned prefix to 256 tokens for your workload.
[06:12] Michael: can you commit the tuned config to the repo?
[06:16] Riley: yes i'll push the tuned batch_profile.json and add README notes about expected tradeoffs.
[06:22] Dana: switching to upgrades — what's the upgrade cadence for runtime patches in pilot? we don't want surprise restarts.
[06:30] Riley: we do rolling upgrades with canaries. for pilot we'll schedule minor runtime patches after hours and provide a 48-hour maintenance notice. major migrations we coordinate with your infra.
[06:42] Michael: that cadence works. please keep maintenance windows off our peak times.
[06:48] Samir: on commercial — if the mid-May perf and security checks pass we can propose a short dedicated capacity commit for predictable throughput. i'll send a pricing deck.
[06:58] Dana: what's the SLA on dedicated?
[07:02] Samir: dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; i'll include the SLOs and the differences between dedicated and hosted in the deck.
[07:10] Michael: minor ask — can we get a breakdown of token cost vs infra cost for the pilot? helps our internal chargeback.
[07:18] Samir: yes, we'll include token-level cost, GPU hourly, and expected amortized per-request cost in the pricing blob.
[07:26] Priya: on audit logs — retention options matter. do you offer immutable retention and export to our SIEM?
[07:34] Riley: yes, audit logs can be exported to your S3 or pushed via syslog to your SIEM; immutability depends on your S3 lifecycle/policy. we'll include recommended configs.
[07:46] Dana: we had one intermittent auth failure last week — it resolved after a retry but i'd like to trace the flow.
[07:54] Michael: that happened when we rotated keys in the KMS test. we might have a short window where principals aren't granted.
[08:02] Riley: will add a checklist for key rotation to avoid auth gaps.
[08:06] Samir: ok let's capture action items and owners.
[08:12] Dana: sounds good.
[08:16] Samir: recap: (1) Riley to push tuned batch config and quant notes and config file into repo; (2) Samir to send security pack including SOC2 extract, KMS policy snippets, and CIDR ranges; (3) Michael to share traceroutes, peering logs and redacted eval prompts; (4) Schedule 10k perf run next Tuesday (Redwood to reserve nodes) and confirm peering before run.
[08:40] Michael: i'll aim to have artifacts by Monday.
[08:44] Priya: compliance will review security pack and we may have follow-up Qs on KMS principals.
[08:50] Samir: totally fine, we'll be responsive. any blockers?
[08:54] Dana: not from my side. thanks for the detailed notes.
[08:58] Riley: one last thing — i'll also include a short troubleshooting checklist for 502s and routing issues.
[09:04] Samir: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the thread with links. bye.
[47:20] (end of recording)
